passages.title: The Paper Boat by the Library
passages.text:
On Monday morning, Aarav reached school early and noticed a small puddle beside the library door. A paper boat floated in it. The boat was made from a page of an old notebook, and someone had drawn a bright red flag on its side.

Aarav wanted to pick it up, but the bell rang. He hurried to class and kept thinking about the boat. At break time, he returned to the library. The puddle had grown because rainwater was dripping from a loose pipe above the door. The paper boat had moved close to a drain.

Aarav called his friend Leela. “We should stop it before it disappears,” he said. Leela found a long twig near the garden and gently guided the boat away from the drain. Then they placed it on a dry bench.

The librarian, Mrs Sen, came outside carrying a small toolbox. She thanked the children for saving the boat. “I made it for our new display,” she explained. “The display is about how water travels through our town. I wanted the boat to show how rainwater can carry things along.”

Aarav looked at the dripping pipe. “Could we tell the caretaker about this too?” he asked. Mrs Sen nodded. They found the caretaker, who promised to repair the pipe after lunch. He also showed them a small channel that carried rainwater toward the garden instead of letting it collect by the door.

That afternoon, the children helped Mrs Sen set up the display. They placed the paper boat beside a drawing of the town’s drains and garden channels. Leela added a label: “Keep water moving safely.”

When Aarav walked past the library the next morning, the doorway was dry. He smiled at the boat in the display. A small problem had led to a useful discovery, and three people had helped solve it.
